title: 15K4JR3B (Hard Version)
solution: Key observation 1 (geometry): a triangle's doubled area is at most W*H, the width times height of its bounding box. W = x_max - x_min <= |x_max| + |x_min| is at most the total magnitude X of all x-moves, and likewise H <= Y, the total of all y-moves, so the answer is at most X*Y where X + Y = T = sum of 2^{a_i}. The bound is attained: give every x-move to A in the negative direction (A = (-X, 0)), leave B at the origin, give every y-move to C upward (C = (0, Y)); the doubled area is exactly X*Y. So the answer is max X*(T-X) over subset sums X, i.e. the two-way partition of the multiset {2^{a_i}} whose sums are as balanced as possible. Key observation 2 (greedy): because the values are powers of two, sorting them descending and adding each to the currently smaller pile is optimal. Every earlier value is a multiple of the current one, so the running difference D is a multiple of it; if D never returns to 0 after the first element, the largest element exceeds all the rest and must sit alone, and otherwise, after the last time D hits 0 just before element v_j, the signed sum of v_1..v_j is an odd multiple of v_j in any partition (the prefix sum is an even multiple of v_j), so any partition has difference >= v_j - (sum of the tail), which is exactly what greedy achieves. A subset-sum DP over sums is infeasible (T up to 100*2^24 ~ 1.7e9), which is why the power-of-two structure matters. Complexity O(n log n) per test; the answer fits in 64 bits (about 7e17).

solution_check.how: sol.py (sort descending, add to smaller pile, output s1*s2) prints 1, 4, 192, 562950054084608 on the 4 samples, all matching. brute.py: (a) exhaustive geometric brute force enumerating all 12^n assignments of each move to (point, axis, sign) and taking the max |cross product|: 600 random cases with n in 2..5 and a_i in 0..5, plus 40 cases with n=6, all equal to sol.py (validates the bounding-box reduction); (b) exhaustive 2^n subset-partition brute max X*(T-X): 3000 random cases with n in 2..16 and a_i up to 24, all equal to sol.py (validates greedy optimality). Seed 7, 0 mismatches.

notes.solver: greedy: the actual algorithm, largest-first into the smaller pile, optimal for powers of two by the divisibility argument. geometry: the reduction is a triangle-area bound (doubled area <= bounding-box width*height, via the cross product) plus the construction attaining it; this is the step the hard version shares with A1 (where it gives floor(n/2)*ceil(n/2)). subset-sum (0.5): after the reduction the problem IS minimum-difference two-way partition (subset sum closest to T/2), so someone searching balanced partition / subset sum should find it; but the classic sum-indexed DP does not fit (T up to ~1.7e9) and the power-of-two structure makes greedy exact, so confidence is moderate. Rejected: bit-manipulation (values are 1<<a_i, but no bitwise reasoning beyond divisibility of powers of two); sorting (scaffolding for the greedy); constructive-algorithm (the output is a number and the optimal placement is trivial once the bound is known); dynamic-programming / digit-dp (a carry DP over bit positions would work but nobody would write it over the greedy); binary-search-answer (no feasibility check); brute-force (the per-move 12-way choice is only the stress-test oracle). Differs from A1 (all steps 1, closed form) in that the step sizes 2^{a_i} turn it into a partition problem.
notes.skeptic: Solution: correct, and the same as mine. The bounding-box bound gives max X*(T-X), and the greedy is exact on powers of two. O(n log n) per test, and the answer fits in a signed 64-bit integer (about 7.2e17 at most). PATTERNS. greedy KEEP (0.9): this is the whole algorithm. It is a real greedy: largest-first into the smaller pile is exact only because each power divides all larger ones, and it is not optimal for general values. geometry KEEP (0.8): the reduction is a triangle-area fact (a triangle has at most half its bounding box's area) plus the triangle inequality on coordinates. This is the step A2 shares with A1, and A1 kept geometry at 0.85. subset-sum KEEP (0.5), which the brief asked me to rule on. After the reduction the problem is minimum-difference two-way partition, i.e. subset sum nearest T/2. That is the shape a 'balanced partition / partition into two subsets with minimum difference' searcher has in mind, and this problem is a useful hit for them: it is the power-of-two special case, where the sum-indexed DP is infeasible (T up to about 1.7e9) and greedy is exact. The corpus already uses subset-sum as a problem-shape label for records that run no sum-indexed DP: codeforces-1840-b Binary Cafe (subset sums of distinct powers of two, read off the binary structure), codeforces-618-f Double Knapsack (pigeonhole), and cses-1628 / cses-3425 (meet-in-the-middle). So it is not reserved for the DP. It is not a statement-word echo either, since the statement never mentions subsets or partitions. The confidence stays at 0.5 because a searcher who wants subset-sum DP practice gets a greedy problem. Is there a better partition-specific label? No. partition-dp in this corpus means DP that cuts a sequence into contiguous segments (Allocate Mailboxes, Largest Sum of Averages, Coding Company), which is a different idea, and nothing here is contiguous or DP. knapsack, subset-dp and bitmask-dp all imply a DP that is not run. subset-sum is the closest label in the vocabulary. REJECTED (agreeing with the proposal): bit-manipulation (1 << a_i is only how the values are written; the argument is divisibility, not bitwise), sorting (scaffolding for the greedy), constructive-algorithm (the output is a number and the optimal placement is a one-line tightness witness, the same ruling as A1), dynamic-programming / digit-dp (a carry DP over bit positions works, but nobody would write it instead of the greedy), and brute-force (only the stress oracle). Also considered and rejected: exchange-argument (greedy optimality comes from a divisibility and odd-multiple argument on the running difference, not from swapping adjacent choices) and number-theory (divisibility of powers of two is too thin for it). MANHATTAN-DISTANCE, checked against A1: not added, and this is a principled difference, not an inconsistency. A1 kept it at 0.5 because unit steps make each vertex cost its L1 distance, so the configurations are exactly 'total L1 at most n'; the brief there noted that a Euclidean budget would change the answer. In A2 the step sizes are fixed and indivisible, so the reachable configurations are not an L1 ball: they are signed subset sums. The only thing that carries over is 'each move goes to one axis', which is the X/Y split that geometry and subset-sum already cover. Nobody would describe A2 as a Manhattan-distance problem, and the hard part is the partition, not a metric. TRAP 1, binary-search-answer: does not apply and was not proposed. There is no feasibility predicate over the answer. X is found directly by the greedy, and searching over candidate X would need a subset-sum oracle, which is the hard part anyway. TRAP 2, bitmask-dp vs DP near-misses: the constraint decides it. The corpus's other minimum-difference partition, cses-1623 Apple Division (n <= 20, arbitrary weights), is bitmask enumeration and is labelled bitmask-dp. Here n <= 100 rules out 2^n, and a_i <= 24 with n <= 100 makes T about 1.7e9, which rules out a sum-indexed bitset DP within 1 s. Only the power-of-two greedy fits. Labelling this bitmask-dp or knapsack would be the careless twin label. TAGS: math, geometry and greedy are fine. array stays: the input is an array, and it is the corpus-wide input-type tag (404 of 1584 CF records), so it is convention, not padding. SUMMARY: the proposal's summary was accurate, 70 words, and had the constraints. It said 'splitting the powers of two into two groups' without saying the groups are the x-moves and the y-moves, which is the key reduction. The rewrite (69 words) states the bound as x-move total times y-move total and keeps 'balanced partition (subset sum nearest half)' and 'greedily largest-first' as search terms. That rewrite is the only change; the patterns and tags are approved as proposed.
